behaviors.behavior: AC-D1: resolve_ci_verification -> no_record classifies as no_qualifying_run, never conflated with run_not_verified
AC-D3: .status == error classifies as verification_query_failed, never proceeding to execution evidence
AC-D4: verified structural verification + execution evidence unavailable classifies as execution_evidence_unavailable
AC-D5: verified structural verification + execution evidence error classifies as execution_evidence_query_failed
AC-D6: confirmed evidence, all bound links green -> gate_confirmed_clean
AC-D7: verified evidence overrides the committed file's own self-reported status
AC-D8: a link absent from verified evidence is fail-closed not_run, reaching gate_violated
AC-D9: link-id matching is scoped per requirement key, not globally
AC-D10: resolve_execution_evidence is never called when verification did not return verified
AC-D11: duplicate verified link ids within one requirement raise ReadError; a verified link with missing/non-string status/executed is treated as absent, not written as raw None
AC-D12: classify_commit resolves the first parent internally (no caller-supplied parent); a root commit raises ReadError

AC-D13: not independently re-tested at this module's boundary -- classify_commit does not branch on WHY no_record was returned, only THAT it was; the pull_request-only scenario is already tested at the resolver boundary
behaviors.reason: shared/tests/test_ci_provenance.py::test_no_record_when_only_pull_request_runs_exist already exercises this scenario at the resolver's own boundary; a duplicate test here would mock the resolver away and be functionally identical to AC-D1's test (external code review round 2, glm, medium -- the original hollow test was removed).

behaviors.behavior: AC-D14: commit is canonicalized to a full SHA (via the ^{commit} peel suffix) before any resolver call; the canonical value reaches both resolvers and both manifest reads; an unresolvable ref raises ReadError
AC-D15: either resolver returning a status outside its own documented contract raises ReadError rather than falling through to the next branch
build_verified_manifest returns a full independent deep copy -- no shared mutable state with the input anywhere in the returned tree

surface_verification.justification: Pure backend library module (classify_commit / build_verified_manifest) with no API routes, store mutations, SSE/WS handlers, or UI-consumed contracts -- consumed only by a future CLI/wiring not yet built (architecture review scope reduction). No startable surface exists to drive.
